Paul Papalia has announced he will quit politics, triggering a by-election for his seat of Secret Harbour. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Long-serving minister Paul Papalia has announced his resignation from politics due to a serious illness affecting an immediate family member.

His resignation will trigger a by-election in the southern Perth seat of Secret Harbour which could open the door to One Nation.

Mr Papalia's last day is Friday, with Labor MPs called to a caucus meeting to elect a replacement minister at that point.

Senior WA government minister and Labor stalwart Paul Papalia has announced his resignation from politics, triggering a by-election in the southern Perth seat of Secret Harbour that could open the door to a resurgent One Nation.

The ABC has confirmed Labor MPs have been summoned to a caucus meeting on Friday, where it is understood a new minister will be elected.

Paul Papalia delivers his prepared speech standing next to the premier. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Mr Papalia's confirmed his retirement at a press conference on Monday afternoon, following months of speculation.

"This isn't what I planned," Mr Papalia said.

"One of my immediate family members has been diagnosed with a serious illness.

"I can't continue to give this role everything it demands while also giving my family what they need from me.

"For most of my married life, my family has sacrificed their interest in favour of my services."

Paul Papalia and the premier hug after his retirement speech. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Mr Papalia's wide-ranging portfolios encompass corrective services, defence industries, emergency services, veterans and racing and gaming.

He was first elected to state parliament in 2007 and has been one of the WA government's most recognisable faces, responsible for a range of hot-button issues including AUKUS, youth detention and emergency responses to cyclones and bushfires.

He said he was particularly proud of his work in defence.

"We've taken it from a neglected afterthought to the key driver of the economy, on its way to being the second biggest sector in the state," he said.

Mr Papalia easily retained Secret Harbour at last year's state election, with an 11.5 per cent margin — but that number was significantly down on the 31.3 per cent margin he previously held.

Paul Papalia has held a range of ministerial portfolios, including emergency services. (ABC News: Samantha Goerling)

And while One Nation polled just 8.4 per cent of the vote in 2025, rapid growth in support for the party in national polls has buoyed the local branch's hopes in the by-election Mr Papalia's departure will trigger.

It comes after One Nation scored a historic win in the federal by-election for the New South Wales seat of Farrer, with David Farley becoming the party's first-ever candidate to be elected to the House of Representatives.

But a local poll conducted by DemosAU in early June found Labor remained the most popular party in the state, followed by the Liberals and One Nation in third with 18 per cent of the primary vote.

WA Labor said a preselection process would now take place with nominations for candidates opening today.

Premier Roger Cook said Mr Papalia's resignation would not trigger a major cabinet restructure.

"The departure of Paul will mean we'll need allocation of portfolios, and we'll make sure that we can communicate that in the days following the caucus meeting," he said.

The WA Liberals have called a meeting for Thursday evening to decide if they will run in the Secret Harbour by election, although it's widely expected they will.

"I see no reason though why we wouldn't be running and running hard," Mr Zempilas told reporters on Monday afternoon.

Mr Papalia enforced a "tough on crime" approach when he was police minister, leading the introduction of WA's stringent knife laws and the biggest changes to the state's firearms laws in decades.

But after the troubled rollout of the firearms laws, he lost the police portfolio, and he faced considerable scrutiny as corrective services minister when two teenage boys died in custody in WA in the space of 12 months.

Paul Papalia's resignation comes a year and four months into WA Labor's third term. (ABC News: James Carmody)

While conditions in detention have improved significantly since he took on the job, he has also overseen a significant increase in overcrowding in the state's adult prisons.

Before entering politics, Mr Papalia was a navy clearance diver who served in the counter-terrorist squadron of the SAS and in Iraq, eventually leaving the armed forces in 2004.

He spent a few years running a small business before joining the Labor Party.

Mr Papalia is currently WA's longest-serving lower house MP.
